notes: Three copilot lifetimes back-to-back: variant 1 (clean /exit) → variant 2 (SIGKILL mid-idle) → variant 3 (SIGKILL mid-turn). Each variant's process_exited anchors the next variant's birth. PROVISIONAL — no copilot recording exists yet. The birth phases are deliberately UNPINNED (no same_session_as, and vN_turn_start does not claim to be the same row) because copilot creates its session directory at launch but events.jsonl only at the first prompt: a proc-<PID> pre-session is likely but not guaranteed to be sampled in that window (scanner polls 1s, backing off to 5s), and when events.jsonl does appear it already holds session.start … user.message, so whether the real session is first observed ready or straight into working is a race unsettleable from source. Everything the scenario actually asserts is pinned to the real session via same_session_as on vN_turn_start: v1 'State is ready at exit' (v1_turn_done → v1_exit); v2 'state never re-enters working/waiting once idle'; v3 'process exits while still working'. No post-kill sweep-to-ready is asserted for v3 — that is a live-dashboard property of the ongoing sweep and gemini-cli's recording showed it falling outside a bounded tail. model is NOT pinned: --model accepts only auto and the router resolves gpt-5-mini or claude-haiku-4.5 at runtime, so record fills it from the recording.

text: Variant 1: a copilot session appears in ready (this may be the proc-<PID> pre-session the scanner mints while events.jsonl does not yet exist, or the real session — deliberately unpinned)
Variant 1: the first user prompt drives ready → working (user.message)
Variant 1: assistant.turn_end settles the session back to ready
Variant 1: clean /exit — process_exited fires AFTER the state returned to ready (the v1_turn_done → v1_exit chain proves 'State is ready at exit')
Variant 2: a new session appears in ready after variant 1 finishes
Variant 2: the user prompt drives ready → working
Variant 2: turn completes back to ready and the idle window begins; through the SIGKILL the session never re-enters working or waiting (satisfies 'state never entered working post-exit')
Variant 2: SIGKILL mid-idle — process_exited fires while the session is in ready
Variant 3: a new session appears in ready after variant 2 finishes
Variant 3: the user prompt drives ready → working

Variant 3: SIGKILL mid-turn — process_exited fires while the session is still working. No post-kill ready phase is asserted: the sweep-to-ready is a live property that may fall outside the recording's 12 s tail (gemini-cli's did).
